fields.statement: QA cycle 1 at 0e9f6a6e, scratch build in a scratch repo (RHIZA_* unset): 'Builds on @other, me@x.org, checkout@v7, '@key', @@lit, (@local) [@<24-char ID prefix>]' stored @{<other ID>}, @{<local ID>} and @{<other ID>} for the three references, kept the email, checkout@v7 and '@key' as written and stored @@lit as @lit; show printed '@renamed ... @@lit ... (@local) [@renamed]' after a rename; an ambiguous 4-char prefix @01M6 and @{BOGUS} were unresolved. go test ./internal/textref passes. Not passing: a write of @@{<26-char ID>} stores @{<ID>}, which Format and check then treat as a reference (see the qa finding).

QA cycle 1 at 0e9f6a6e, scratch build in a scratch repo: rhiza add stored @handle, an ID prefix and a node of its own change set as @{<full ID>}; @foreign (another unlanded change set), @nosuch, @{BOGUS} and a newly referenced retired node were refused with exit 4, code not_found, naming each reference and field, next 'fix the handle, or write @@ for a literal @', also under --dry-run, and wrote nothing; rhiza apply with a good item plus a bad one refused the whole file (good not created) and an apply add resolved @other; after retiring gone, set of holder's statement keeping @{<gone ID>} was kept while adding it to another node or to holder's acceptance was refused; quote, quote_where and wording, and a source's summary and title were stored verbatim. Lenient engine writes: note add 'Seen @renamed and @nosuch' stored @{<ID>} and a literal @nosuch, shown @@nosuch; question answer 'Use @renamed, not @ghost' stored statement 'Use @{<ID>}, not @ghost' and the quote verbatim. rhiza guide tells agents to write @handle and @@.

QA cycle 1 at 0e9f6a6e, scratch build in a scratch repo: after other was renamed to renamed, show, why, slice, search, change show and change diff printed @renamed in text and --json; search '@renamed' found the node; after landing, rhiza render wrote @renamed into capability/one.md; tui app show/why/slice one --once printed @renamed. A retired reference showed @{<full ID>} and writing it back with set stored the same text; writing one's shown statement back stored the same IDs and literal @. A hand-edited log entry 'Old @word and @{ID}' showed 'Old @@word and @@{ID}' and writing that back stored the same literal text; 'Lit @@word' stored 'Lit @word' and showed '@@word'. Verbatim quote fields and a source's summary print raw. (Hand-editing an entry needs a fresh XDG_CACHE_HOME: the existing index cache keys by entry.)

QA cycle 1 at 0e9f6a6e, scratch build in a scratch repo: a hand-forged @{01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ} in a log entry made rhiza check exit 1 with 'fail text-ref ... legacy field statement holds @{01ZZ...}, which names no node' (and rule text-ref in --json); a reference to a retired node gave a warn while check stayed ok; text-ref appears in describe --json; go test ./internal/check passes. FAIL: rhiza check on this repo at the branch head (make self-check) fails with 'fail text-ref change set 01M6HNNWFR1J2AHQRNKFTPME46: text-ref-check-verified field statement holds @{01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ}, which names no node'; in a scratch repo, rhiza add with 'a forged @@{01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ} here' succeeds and then rhiza check fails the same way.
